comment: song_id -> extracted file, the ROM's ordering for it, and the evidence for naming one. Entries are sorted by (player, song_id), which is the ROM's own grouping -- see `ordering`. Every stem still carries the ROM's numbering, so the music tier reads Extracted and not Named. That is not an extraction gap: a name has to say what the sound IS, and neither the sound table nor the sequence bytes say that. `played_by` is the only linkage that could name one: the owners whose reconstructed C calls Func_080f9010 -- the linker veneer to the engine dispatcher Func_080f9080, whose first argument is the song id -- with this id as a LITERAL. 52 such sites across 34 ids; 22 of those ids have exactly one caller. A further 41 owners call the dispatcher with a computed id and cannot be attributed, and no overlay calls it with a literal. NAMING IS BLOCKED, and the reason is measured rather than assumed: the corpus has established 341 descriptive identities, and ZERO of them are reachable from any sound caller. They are all overlay-local Func_02xxxxxx aliases while every caller of the dispatcher is a main-image Func_08xxxxxx. So `played_by` says 'this id is played from there' and nothing more -- not what it sounds like, not which scene owns it. Naming waits on main-image caller identities, which is ordinary decompilation and not audio work. Do not invent names to move the tier. Derived from games/gs1/src/ and games/gs1/assets/audio/song_table.json; regenerate rather than editing by hand.

accounting.note: 312 = 260 extracted + 4 per-song empty headers + 48 table slots pointing at the shared sound_empty at 0x080fd044. Checked against residuals_index.json: all four empty ids are listed there, so the four entries with a null file are accounted for and are not extraction gaps.

ordering.note: The ROM's own ordering, not an imposed one. Every entry in the sound table at 0x080fc684 carries a player number beside its header pointer, and that number partitions the 312 slots exactly: players 0 and 1 hold all 58 music sequences, players 2 through 7 all 202 effects, with no exception either way. So the `class` field is confirmed ROM-derived rather than a heuristic on track counts. A player is a voice-allocation group in the m4a engine, so two sounds on different players can sound together and two on the same player cannot -- which is why the grouping is worth carrying.
ordering.duplicate_sequences: none: all 260 extracted sequences are byte-distinct (sha1 over the .mid)

axes.player: The partition. Players 0-1 carry all 58 extracted music sequences, 2-7 all 202 effects, no exception. A player is a voice-allocation group, so two sounds on one player cannot overlap.
axes.priority: The engine's own precedence: Func_080faa58 refuses to start a song whose priority does not beat the playing one. All 60 music headers are priority 0. Effects are 100 for 187 of them, with 90 on one, 110 on thirteen and 120 on two -- so those sixteen are the sounds meant to cut through, and that is an ordering the ROM states rather than one inferred.
axes.tone_bank: Exactly two banks across all 264 headers, and they partition by class perfectly: 0x080fba78 for all 60 music, 0x080fc138 for all 204 effects. This is the third independent ROM axis agreeing with `class` and `player`, which is why the music/effect split can be stated as fact rather than as a track-count heuristic. The two banks are also the only audio objects here that CAN be named from evidence -- they are the instrument sets a .sf2 extraction would produce, one for music and one for effects.
axes.reverb: Bit 7 gates the reverb call in Func_080faa58. All 60 music headers carry 178 (bit 7 set). Effects carry 0 for 188 and 128 for 16, so those sixteen take reverb where the rest do not.

wave_attribution.note: Which tone bank uses each PCM sample, and at which MIDI program. Read from the two banks in the ROM -- 12-byte m4a tone entries, the word at +4 being the wave pointer -- and joined to games/gs1/assets/audio/waves/index.json by address. The split is clean: wave_00..wave_13 are music instruments, wave_20..wave_31 effect samples. wave_14..wave_19 resolve from neither bank directly, because a tone entry of type 0x40 or 0x80 points at a keysplit or percussion sub-table instead of a wave, and those were not followed. Recorded HERE and not in waves_index.json, which is a build input read by build-assets and pinned by tools/audio-wave/tests/real_assets.rs; this file is read by no tool, so extending it cannot break the build. This is attribution, not a name: it says a sample is the music bank's program 8, not what instrument that is.

layout.sequences: games/gs1/assets/audio/sequences/ -- index.json plus BGM_<id>.mid or SE_<id>.mid and optional sidecar
layout.note: Both folders are derived, not decorative: build-assets takes the sequence directory from the index's own parent, and the wave prefix from the index's filename with `index.json` stripped. Moving each index into a folder named for its contents therefore moved the assets with it and left the wave prefix empty, which is why `waves_wave_00.pcm8.wav` became `waves/wave_00.pcm8.wav` with no code change. The manifest already declared `games/gs1/assets/audio/waves/residual/index.json` for a pending package, so this is the layout that was intended.

naming.note: Audio names follow the ROM channel identities BGM_<id>, SE_<id>, and wave_<id>. Only call-site-proven sound effects receive terse semantic SE names.
